title: UPDATE: OpenAI Adds Prompt Presets to Codex CLI and Updates Reasoning Cache
summary:
OpenAI released a software update for its Codex and Work tools that allows developers to adjust reasoning levels mid-conversation without clearing the prompt cache. The change enables users to switch to lower reasoning for simple tasks and increase it for complex ones without reprocessing the conversation history, reducing the need to rebuild context.

The company also updated the Codex CLI to version 0.164.0, introducing reusable prompt presets that save model and reasoning settings for recall via /presets or Ctrl X P. The CLI release includes inline model and permission changes, fixes for long session resumes, and support for Windows proxy authentication and Enterprise MCP sign-in. Additionally, connection speeds have been increased for persistent agents known as dots.

QoL update for Codex devs:

You can now switch reasoning levels mid-conversation without losing your cache! Use lower reasoning for the quick stuff and dial it up when you need it, without having to rebuild the context.

and some nice CLI updates:

- Reusable prompt presets
- Change models and permissions inline
- Fixes for resuming long sessions
- Enterprise MCP sign-in and Windows proxy auth

Also dot calls connect much faster now too ;)

You can now choose 12-hour prompt caching in the API.

Persistent agents, like dots, reuse context throughout the day. 

You can keep shared instructions, tools, and context cached longer and pay the lower cached-input rate, even when requests are hours apart.
